original_question: Does every height-three complete intersection have the strong Lefschetz property? More generally, does the same hold for complete intersections of larger height, for example Artinian complete intersections of height four?
target_in_paper: Section 2, Question 2.2 (Complete Intersections): "Does every height three complete intersection has the SLP? Is this true for complete intersections of larger height, e.g., Artinian height four?"
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper’s actual target. It correctly asks about the strong Lefschetz property (not merely the weak Lefschetz property), correctly singles out height-three complete intersections, and correctly retains the paper’s immediate higher-height follow-up by mentioning the Artinian height-four case. In substance, it is essentially a paraphrase of Question 2.2.
missing_details: The paper imposes a standing hypothesis for Section 2: unless stated otherwise, the ground field is of characteristic zero.
The intended objects are graded complete intersections coming from homogeneous ideals in a polynomial ring K[x1, ..., xn], viewed through the Artinian quotient A = K[x1, ..., xn]/I.

For the first clause, Artinianity is implicit from the Lefschetz-property setting and the surrounding discussion, even though the short official wording says only "height three complete intersection."

To be stand-alone, the question should specify that I is a homogeneous complete intersection ideal (equivalently, generated by a homogeneous regular sequence), so that A is a standard graded Artinian complete intersection.
The strong Lefschetz property should be defined explicitly: there exists a linear form ℓ in A1 such that for all integers i, d >= 0, the multiplication map ×ℓ^d : Ai -> A(i+d) has maximal rank.
The phrase "larger height" should remain in the same Artinian graded complete-intersection setting; otherwise it becomes broader than the paper’s question.
No uniform-degree assumption should be added: that belongs to the separate, more specific Question 2.3, not Question 2.2.
No extra hypotheses about monomial bases, special generators, positive characteristic, or nonstandard gradings belong here; those are different nearby problems.
refined_question: Let K be a field of characteristic 0, let R = K[x1, ..., xn], and let I ⊂ R be a homogeneous complete intersection ideal such that A = R/I is a standard graded Artinian complete intersection. If ht(I) = 3, must A have the strong Lefschetz property; that is, does there exist a linear form ℓ ∈ A1 such that for every i, d >= 0 the multiplication map ×ℓ^d : Ai -> A(i+d) has maximal rank? More generally, is the same true for Artinian complete intersections of larger height, already for ht(I) = 4?
justification: The nearest official formulation is exactly Section 2, Question 2.2. I did not replace it by the broader Question 2.1, which asks about WLP/SLP for every complete intersection in any number of variables, and I did not narrow it to Question 2.3, which adds a uniform-degree and monomial-basis hypothesis. Your draft matches Question 2.2 almost verbatim, so that is the correct target. To make it fully stand-alone and faithful to the paper, I restored the Section 2 standing assumption that the field has characteristic zero, made explicit the homogeneous polynomial-ring quotient A = R/I that underlies Lefschetz questions in this section, and spelled out the quantified definition of SLP. The chapter containing this material is the Springer version of arXiv:2311.03081, pp. 211–225, and the complete-intersection questions appear at the start of Section 2.
